evaluation_protocol.rule_if_new_capability_is_needed: record the V0.12 external case as not certified; the capability may be developed only in a later version such as V0.13

excluded: any project represented in V0.11/V0.12 development evidence
any exact source body SHA-256 appearing in historical evidence
tests, examples and benchmark-only helper code
functions selected after examining BIZPROOF certification outcomes
required: project identity absent from the complete historical development provenance set
project source snapshot frozen before any candidate certification outcome is observed
at least 10 eligible non-trivial Python functions or methods
source file and function body hashable deterministically

external_validation_role: prospective untouched project-level external generalization cohort

function_selection.deficit_rule: if a project contains fewer than two eligible functions in a stratum, select all available in that stratum and fill the remaining project slots from the project's still-unselected eligible functions by the same deterministic hash ranking

shape_strata.description: local scalar/control semantics without nested functions, explicit state writes or domain/vector operators
mapping, sequence, comprehension, container projection or structured return
nested functions, comprehensions, higher-order transformations or vector/domain operators
observable state mutation, attribute/item write, persistence-style call or ordered effect semantics
parameter/entity binding, external framework dependency, enums, dates or multi-object domain semantics

function_selection.stratum_assignment: computed only from source/AST/dependency shape before BIZPROOF certification
function_selection.within_stratum_selection: ascending SHA256(seed || project identity || relative source path || function qualified name || source SHA256)

project_selection.rule: rank all eligible unseen projects ascending by deterministic hash and select the first 12

sample_size_rationale.failure_detection_example: if the true independent case-level failure rate were 5%, 120 observations give approximately 99.8% probability of observing at least one failure; this is descriptive, not a power claim under arbitrary dependence
sample_size_rationale.interpretation: large enough for project-level holdout analysis while retaining tractable exact-source replay and formal mutant validation

secondary_endpoints: certification yield by frozen source-shape stratum
mutant refutation success rate where A2 is attempted
